The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. This pangram contains every letter of the
English alphabet at least once. Pangrams are often used to display typefaces or test
keyboards and other equipment. The sentence has been used since at least the late
nineteenth century and is still widely recognized today.

Language is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary.
It is the primary means by which humans convey meaning, both through spoken and written
forms. Every human culture that has ever been studied has been found to have a fully
developed language. Some estimates suggest there are between six and seven thousand
languages currently spoken around the world.

The history of writing spans more than five thousand years. The earliest known writing
system is cuneiform, developed by the Sumerians of ancient Mesopotamia around 3400 BCE.
Hieroglyphic writing in ancient Egypt followed shortly after. These early scripts began
as pictographic systems and gradually became more abstract over time.

A document is a written, drawn, presented, or memorialized representation of thought.
Originating from the Latin Documentum meaning lesson or proof, it is closely related
to the Latin verb Docere which means to teach. In the past, the word was usually
used to denote a written proof useful as evidence of a truth or fact.

Information retrieval is the activity of obtaining information system resources that
are relevant to an information need from a collection of those resources. Searches can
be based on full-text or other content-based indexing. Information retrieval is the
science of searching for information in a document, searching for documents themselves,
and also searching for the metadata that describes data, and for databases of texts,
images or sounds.

Natural language processing is a subfield of linguistics, computer science, and artificial
intelligence concerned with the interactions between computers and human language, in
particular how to program computers to process and analyze large amounts of natural
language data. The goal is a computer capable of understanding the contents of documents,
including the contextual nuances of the language within them.

Machine learning is a method of data analysis that automates analytical model building.
It is based on the idea that systems can learn from data, identify patterns and make
decisions with minimal human intervention. Machine learning algorithms are trained on
datasets to find patterns and make predictions, improving accuracy over time as they
process more data.

Embedding is a relatively low-dimensional space into which you can translate
high-dimensional vectors. Embeddings make it easier to do machine learning on large
inputs like sparse vectors representing words. An embedding captures some of the
semantics of the input by placing semantically similar inputs close together in the
embedding space.

Vector databases are purpose-built to handle the unique structure of vector embeddings.
They index vectors for fast retrieval and can find similar vectors efficiently using
approximate nearest neighbor algorithms. These databases are increasingly important for
applications that use large language models, since they enable fast semantic search
across large collections of documents.

Chunking is the process of breaking large documents into smaller pieces for indexing.
The optimal chunk size depends on the use case and the embedding model being used.
Smaller chunks allow for more precise retrieval but may lose context. Larger chunks
preserve context but reduce precision. Overlapping chunks help bridge boundaries.
